channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: US Rebukes Australia for Plan to Target Social Media Algorithms
item.description: The US government criticized Australia’s plan to clamp down on social media algorithms and harmful content online, opening up a fresh political front in Canberra’s campaign to get tougher on Big Tech.
item.dc:creator: Angus Whitley

item.title: SB Energy Plans to Start IPO Marketing After SEC Review Finished
item.description: SB Energy, the SoftBank Group Corp.-backed energy company that’s now building data centers, is preparing to start formally marketing its initial public offering to investors once US regulators are finished reviewing the company’s IPO filing, people familiar with the plan said.
item.dc:creator: Mark Chediak

item.title: India’s Titan On What's Slowing Gold Demand
item.description: Titan's Managing Director Ajoy Chawla says gold rate volatility, and not the macros has been the biggest challenge for the company in recent times. He said this in an exclusive conversation with BTV's Menaka Doshi. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Foxconn of India: Dixon Tech Eyes Growth Beyond Smartphones
item.description: Sunil Vachani, executive chairman of Dixon Technologies, India's leading electronics manufacturing services company, talks about slow demand for smartphones, production incentives, revenue diversification and China investments in an exclusive conversation with BTV's Menaka Doshi. Vachani also discusses how India can move from assembly to value-added manufacturing. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Aldi US COO: Americans Are Feeling Inflation Pressures
item.description: Dave Rinaldo, Aldi US Chief Operating Officer, joins Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick to breakdown shopping trends he's seeing in the US consumer, the grocer's plan to open 180 stores by year-end and its new digital strategy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Whole Foods CEO: Customers Are Making More Trips
item.description: Whole Foods CEO Jason Buechel came into the studio to speak with Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick about Amazon's approach to affordability, how customer's are changing shopping habits amid rising costs and how the healthy grocery competition has changed. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Qualcomm CFO on Snapdragon and Two New Mobile Platforms
item.description: Qualcomm shares rose 2% as the company opened its Snapdragon Summit and unveiled two new flagship mobile platforms. Akash Palkhiwala says the event is focused on bringing Qualcomm’s technology into hundreds of millions of devices over the next few years, with a major emphasis on “agentic AI.” He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: DWS Group CEO on International Investment Opportunities
item.description: Stefan Hoops, CEO of DWS Group Global, discusses the case for diversification and where U.S.-based investors might look for it. Hoops argued that investors should consider spreading risk beyond the U.S. and beyond the AI trade, saying Europe offers opportunities in industries outside of the AI stack. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Bailey Lipschultz on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Tech Trade Is Just Fine, CVC Marathon's Richards Says
item.description: Bruce Richards, managing partner and head of CVC Marathon, says the technology trade is still “just fine” even as published private credit default rates rise. Speaking on "Bloomberg The Close," Richards argues that higher-for-longer rates have created an attractive environment for investors because they are getting better risk-adjusted returns in both investment-grade and non-investment-grade debt. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Singapore Wants AI to Shop But With Strict Limits, Study Shows
item.description: Singaporeans are among the most open to allowing an artificial intelligence agent to shop for them but they also want the strictest guardrails, research shows.
item.dc:creator: Rosalind Mathieson

item.title: Clarity Fails, SEC's Tokenization Green Light
item.description: "Bloomberg Crypto" covers the people, transactions, and technology shaping the world of decentralized finance. Today's guests: Circle Chief Strategy Officer & Head of Global Policy Dante Disparte, Strive CEO Matt Cole, SEC Director, Division of Trading & Markets Jamie Selway, Securitize Chairman, Co-Founder & CEO Carlos Domingo, and Independent Community Bankers of American President & CEO Rebeca Romero Rainey. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Clarity Failure A Win For Communities: Romero Rainey
item.description: With the Clarity Act failing in the Senate, stablecoin yields remain outside of US regulation. Independent Community Bankers of America CEO Rebeca Romero Rainey discusses her opposition to the bill with Isabelle Lee and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Cos. Won't Opt-Out of Tokenization: Securitize CEO
item.description: Carlos Domingo, chairman, co-founder and CEO of Securitize, joins Isabelle Lee and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." SEC gave the green light for digital versions of securities to start trading in the US. Crypto firms are racing to tokenize US stocks, with different models competing for market share. Some firms, such as Securitize, are working directly with public companies to bring tokenized shares to US crypto markets. Others will provide third-party tokens that don’t involve close cooperation with issuers. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: We Want This Country to Win Tokenization: SEC's Selway
item.description:
The Securities and Exchange Commission gave the green light for digital versions of securities to start trading in the US, moving forward with a plan that could reshape traditional market structure after crypto legislation failed a key Senate vote last week. Jamie Selway, director of the division of trading and markets at the SEC, talks with Isabelle Lee and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto."
(Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: We Want This Country to Win Tokenization: SEC's Selway
item.description: The Securities and Exchange Commission gave the green light for digital versions of securities to start trading in the US, moving forward with a plan that could reshape traditional market structure after crypto legislation failed a key Senate vote last week. Jamie Selway, director of the division of trading and markets at the SEC, talks with Isabelle Lee and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bitcoin 'Go to Moon', DATs Not Broken: Strive CEO
item.description: Matt Cole CEO of Strive, joins Isabelle Lee and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." Digital assets have reclaimed $3 trillion in market value for the first time since January after Bitcoin’s stunning rally, but traders are also piling into leveraged bets in perpetual futures, increasing the risk of rapid price swings. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ari Emanuel Dishes on Hollywood Feuds, Paramount Merger and Elon Musk Friendship
item.description: A conversation with the pugilistic and hyperactive media mogul about his new memoir ‘Roll the Calls’
item.dc:creator: Lucas Shaw

item.title: World Labs Founder Fei-Fei Li Urges Independent Oversight of AI
item.description: Artificial intelligence pioneer Fei-Fei Li called for more oversight of the technology by independent and public-sector entities, arguing that safety assessments of increasingly capable AI systems shouldn’t be left solely to the companies developing them.
item.dc:creator: Micah Barkley

item.title: SEC, CFTC No Sub for Long-Range Laws: Circle's Disparte
item.description: Dante Disparte, chief strategy officer and head of global policy at Circle, joins Isabelle Lee and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." SEC last week granted a five-year exemption allowing qualifying venues to trade tokenized US stocks onchain. The move came just days after the Clarity Act failed to advance in the Senate, leaving regulators to press ahead with parts of the crypto agenda without new legislation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Andreessen Horowitz Launches AI School as a College Alternative
item.description: Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz is launching a new program aimed at recent high school graduates and college dropouts that will identify and train young talent building artificial intelligence products.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Torrence
